description: IPA-transliterated perception snippets used for zero-shot CE evaluation in the SCiL 2026 v2 paper. Source files renamed from transliteration_{lang}_ipa_{timestamp}.txt to perception_{lang}.txt to match scripts.zero_shot_eval default template.

producing_tool.name: turkic-translit
producing_tool.determined: 2026-08-12, forensically rather than from a record
producing_tool.how: Released rule files were compared against the transcriptions. Every release from 0.3.2 to 0.3.6 is indistinguishable on the discriminating mappings (kk у > u, ky ж > ʒ, ky ц > ʦ) and all are inconsistent with 0.3.7 and later, which map kk у > w. 0.3.6 was the current release on the generation date, so it is the likely one, but the range is what the evidence proves. Ask Moldir to confirm the exact version and whether she installed from PyPI or used the web interface.
producing_tool.note: Hashes are of the 0.3.6 rule files, recorded so a future reader can check a regenerated file against the one that produced these numbers instead of deducing the version again. The version alone would not be enough: the repository and the published release disagreed during this period.

perception_kk.txt.regenerated: 2026-08-12, from the orthographic source in data/perception_sources with turkic-translit 0.5.1, structure verbatim, passage lines only. Diff against the file replaced: 67 tokens changed, all Cyrillic u next to a vowel becoming the glide w; nothing else moved.

perception_ky.txt.regenerated: 2026-08-12, from the orthographic source in data/perception_sources with turkic-translit 0.5.1, structure verbatim, passage lines only. Diff against the file replaced: 138 tokens changed, all the affricate corrections: bare fricative to d-tie-zh for zhe, ligature to tie bar for che; nothing else moved.

perception_tr.txt.note: The soft-g defect fixed in 0.4.0 could have left a length mark with no vowel before it. Checked 2026-08-12: all 64 length marks in this file follow a vowel, so no site in this text was affected.

perception_ug.txt.note: Four Arabic characters were unmapped in 0.3.6 and would have passed through untransliterated. Checked 2026-08-12: none occurs in this file.

perception_uz.txt.regenerated: 2026-08-12, from the orthographic source in data/perception_sources with turkic-translit 0.5.1, structure verbatim, passage lines only. Diff against the file replaced: 33 tokens changed, all jo to j-open-o for <yo>; nothing else moved.

perception_fi.txt.produced_by: Austin Wagner (2026-06-30, regenerated 2026-08-12), IPA rendered via turkic_translit.core.to_ipa with fi_ipa.rules; passage lines only

notes: perception_fi.txt was added 2026-06-30 to enable Turkic-listener-scoring-Finnish-target excess-CE runs. The 20 parallel passages (4 texts x 5 sub-passages, matching the six Turkic sets) were translated into Finnish at B2 register from the source content shared across the Turkic set, saved as perception_fi_source.txt, and transliterated via turkic_translit.core.to_ipa. Reviewed 2026-08-12 against the six native-speaker-checked parallel translations (author-side review, not a native read): no meaning divergences found in the 20 passages, and a numeral audit across all seven versions found zero disagreements; see docs/finnish-translation-review-2026-08-12.md. Reviewed by a native Finnish speaker 2026-08-12: one agreement error and six unnatural phrasings corrected in the source, IPA regenerated and re-harmonised the same day; the Finnish passages now carry the same review level as the Turkic translations.

perception_uz.txt has 19 passages, not 20: TEXT 2 ('Catching a cold') passage 5 was deliberately excluded by Moldir because its audio recording was removed due to speaker disfluency (confirmed 2026-06-12). The model eval correctly scores the 19 passages that human listeners actually heard; do NOT reconstruct the missing passage.

Each file contains multiple TEXT N sections separated by headers and 1..5 section markers; these constitute under 5 percent of total chars and are kept as-is so all seven files share the same metadata pattern.

Char inventory check at receipt: 41-60 unique chars per file, zero Cyrillic leak across all six original Turkic files, Uyghur contains 51 Arabic-script punctuation chars (Arabic comma/question/semicolon) preserved from source orthography. Finnish file inventory: 38 unique chars, all in Suomi et al. 2008 broad phonemic inventory. SCOPE, added 2026-08-12: this check tested for Cyrillic and for the size of the inventory. It cannot see a character that is legal IPA but the wrong value for the letter that produced it, which is what all three superseded entries above are, so it is not evidence that a file is current.

perception_fi.txt was regenerated 2026-08-12. The original passed the whole source file through to_ipa, headers included, and Finnish rules write x as ks, so TEXT became tekst. The evaluator strips title lines matching text or txt, so the Finnish titles were not stripped and were appended to the last passage of the preceding text; 3 of 20 sections were scored with a title attached, about 58 characters of 4333. Only passage lines are transliterated now: the language name, the TEXT headers, the numeric markers and the blank lines are copied verbatim. The header pattern in zero_shot_eval.py was also widened to recognise tekst, and tests/test_perception_files.py asserts against the real files that every language yields its expected section count, that all four title lines are recognised, and that no title survives into a scored section.

Regeneration status, 2026-08-12: three of the seven files were produced by rules since corrected, and the entries above say which and by how much. Regenerating them needs the orthographic sources, which this repository does not hold for the six Turkic languages; only perception_fi_source.txt is here. Until those sources are available the rules cannot be checked against the data at all, which is the gap that let these three go unnoticed. Asking Moldir for the six orthographic originals is what closes it, after which a test can regenerate each file and assert byte-identity.

2026-08-12: kk, ky and uz regenerated from their orthographic sources with 0.5.1; training corpora rebuilt the same day with the same rules (rebuild_2026-08, budget 12,642,807 chars set by uz). The train/eval consistency guard now covers all seven languages with no exemptions.
